claim: Retry() copies Model: orig.Model verbatim with no tier parameter, so 'attempt 3 re-dispatches at the next tier up' requires a new code path (new helper or changed signature), not an incremental extension.

The oscillation guard depends on a 'dispatch chain' that persists escalation count across re-triggers, but ListRetryChain walks ParentDispatchID within the dispatch store; a human re-triggering the same task creates a fresh root dispatch with no ancestry link, silently resetting the 'one escalation per chain' cap to zero.

Phase 3 ships a machine-checkable acceptance-criteria block but nothing verifies a criterion is actually machine-checkable (vs restating 'follows the design') before quality-gates trusts it as a rubric, so the validator's plan-conformance verdict silently degrades back into judgment-based review wearing a checklist.

_routing_model_tier (bash) and ParseModelTier (Go) both fall through to tier 0 for any unrecognized string; if 'fable' is added to routing.yaml config tiers but not to these tier-ranking functions, fable resolves to tier 0, which is < every real safety floor, so any floor-configured agent silently clamps fable down to its floor on the first call.

The plan calls Go-side ParseModelTier 'optional' for Phase 1, but it already exists and is load-bearing in applyFloor, exercised whenever the bash fast-path falls back to Go (CLAVAIN_RUN_ID unset); the two resolvers will silently diverge on fable resolution the moment either is touched without the other.

The CLAVAIN_RUN_ID-gated skip of the Go fast-path is asserted as a load-bearing invariant, but nothing specifies how CLAVAIN_RUN_ID propagates to nested subagent/background/codex-delegate dispatches; if a subshell doesn't inherit it, the Go fast-path (no agency-override support) silently resolves a different model and routing_decisions.rule_matched records a plausible value with no divergence signal.

The escalation ladder has no code-enforced per-dispatch-chain cap or terminal relief valve to a human once fable itself fails; it is filed as an open question, not a phase deliverable, so a chain that escalates to fable, fails, and re-enters at sonnet can re-trigger its own two-strikes counter and escalate to fable again — a standing wave burning the scarcest rationed resource indefinitely.

The fable→opus fallback is committed only for top-level 'session model == fable' detection and 'opus fallback baked into resolution', but the plan doesn't enumerate every inlet where fable can be selected (Go router fast-path, subagent spawns, codex-delegate dispatches that never see the interactive session model), so a spillway exists at the headworks while a downstream side channel still has a plain levee.

retry.go copies Model: orig.Model verbatim and ShouldRetry only checks RetryCount/status, so Phase 2's 'two-strikes escalation' has no forge to build the tier-change onto — a naive extension (wrapper calling Retry 3 times) still produces same-model retries indistinguishable from escalation; the plan must replace the model-copy behavior, not layer on top of it.

Phase 3 describes the plan-conformance fix only as the validator 'receives the criteria as its rubric' without specifying the mechanism that prevents it from also running its normal flux-drive review and blending the two into one verdict; if plan-conformance and review-findings share a gate or scoring function, the fixed-gauge inspection collapses back into 'the master's opinion informed by a checklist' — exactly the Rule 3 failure mode.

The doctrine forbids 'use your judgment' steps in execution-grade plans but this is filed as an open question with no owner or mechanism, so Phases 1-4 can complete and still ship execution-grade plans that silently contain judgment steps handed to a sonnet-tier executor with no calibrated judgment to fall back on.

claim: The oscillation risk is worse than 'no cap' — it is 'no substrate to cap': generateID() mints a fresh random root on every store.Create(), and ParentDispatchID/RetryCount are set only by Retry(); the instant a task is re-triggered as a new top-level dispatch (sprint re-invoke, fresh ic dispatch, new session) the escalation lineage is severed by construction, and ListRetryChain cannot distinguish a genuinely-new task from an exhausted-then-re-tried one.

The minimal viable cap is not a Dispatch field but one persisted key keyed on task identity that outlives the dispatch row: an EscalationChainID derived from <bead-id>:<phase>, counted via intercore_state (mirroring the agency.models.${phase} step-0 read pattern) or a small table with a TerminalAt flag, checked-and-incremented before every dispatch creation (retry OR fresh Create), because dispatch-chain identity provably does not survive the re-trigger case the cap must cover.

claim: Separate from the chain-identity gap, the mechanical seam for tier-stepping does not exist: Retry() hardcodes Model: orig.Model and RetryPolicy has five fields none referencing model/tier, so Phase 2's 'attempt 3 re-dispatches at next tier up' has no policy-driven override point to attach to without a signature change.

The two-strikes escalation spillway is the exact mechanism that populates the per-(author_tier,executor_tier) gating metric's sample, and it does so asymmetrically by construction: every task hard enough to fail sonnet twice is removed from the sonnet-executor population and deposited into opus/fable's, so the natural 'each dispatch's own executor_tier' implementation silently drains sonnet's hardest cases and inflates both tiers' apparent competence simultaneously — the doctrine's own pass-rate premise is unmeasurable until escalated-dispatch attribution is decided, and the plan is silent on it.

claim: Phase 2's escalation ladder re-dispatches WORK but not KNOWLEDGE: Retry() copies orig.PromptFile verbatim (line 116) and explicitly nils VerdictFile (line 119), and there is no interspect import in internal/dispatch/, so the escalated higher tier receives none of the failed attempt's failure mode — while orchestrate.py's build_prompt() (line 313 via summarize_output line 290) already implements exactly 'read a prior verdict, inject into next prompt' but is wired only to the DAG dependency edge, not the retry chain; Phase 2 doesn't route escalation through it.

The one-escalation cap (design considerations line 82) specifies a valid terminal stop condition but not what artifact accompanies surfacing to the human; given no lesson-payload threading and an undifferentiated failure_mode, the likely default surfaces only the final dispatch's own failed output plus a counter, not the per-tier lesson chain (what sonnet tried and why, what opus changed and why that failed too), forcing the human/frontier terminal inspector to re-derive the whole chain by hand — and termination is the one point where the state machine hands control entirely outside itself, exactly where the transmission inheritance obligation is highest.

claim: The proposed fable-window trigger 'treat session model == fable as the signal' (line 80) is the maker self-attesting his own material grade: the session's self-report of 'I am fable' is what loads the capability-routing agency spec that determines who plans, executes, and validates for the entire run, and none of the three candidate mechanisms (env var, probe, static config flip) includes a kernel-side independent verification — so the doctrine's whole tier-separation guarantee (Rule 3, opus validates never its own judgment) rests on tier identity being trustworthy at assignment time via an unverified in-session variable a running model could misreport.

f-017's gap is wider and structural, not merely unconfirmed: at least three independent paths reach a dispatch Model field with zero safety-floor clamp by construction — ResolveDispatchTier (Go) does a bare map lookup with no applyFloor call, ic dispatch spawn --model takes a raw CLI flag straight into SpawnOptions.Model->-m, and CLAVAIN_MODEL env injection sits entirely outside lib-routing.sh; low-risk today only because dispatch.tiers holds Codex IDs, latent the moment a Claude tier alias is added.

Neither _routing_model_tier (bash) nor ParseModelTier (Go) has a 'fable' case today, so an unrecognized tier string is treated as tier 0/TierUnknown; the probe reads Go-side applyFloor as treating TierUnknown as 'skip the floor comparison' (fails OPEN/unclamped) — but the bash side, by numeric comparison (model_tier=0 < any real floor), would instead clamp fable DOWN to the floor. Either way the sequencing hazard holds: if agency-spec wiring lands before the tier tables are updated, a manual test of the fallback path looks correct by coincidence while the general 'fable + floor set' case is wrong, and Phase 1's acceptance criteria have no test for it.

Agent frontmatter model: fields (751 files across .claude/agents, os/Clavain/agents, interflux/agents; 731 sonnet/96 opus/60 inherit/54 haiku) are a fourth, wholly separate selection surface with zero fable value present and no mechanism in Phases 1-4 to route them through ic route model at all — this is Claude Code's native Task-tool subagent model selection, a static per-file literal the routing kernel has no lever over, so 'fable does planning/architecture' does not reach review-agent subagents (e.g. fd-architecture pinned to model: sonnet) unless a future phase covers frontmatter-level routing.

cmdSetArtifact already computes blake3.Sum256 and stores it as ArtifactRecord.BlobHash in CXDB whenever any artifact (including Phase 3's acceptance-criteria file) is registered via set-artifact, but that hash is never read back anywhere in clavain-cli (write-only telemetry, fail-open at every step) and Phase 3/4 reinvent a second, hash-less sealing story for the exact same artifact instead of binding the existing custody witness into plan_execution_outcome — an existing content-addressed seal sits one file away from the measurement surface that needs it, and the plan's authors evidently didn't grep for it.
